comparison: intent pool versus original shared pool
seedPolicy: First listed protocol seed, no best-of-three selection

rows.reason: Vitaforte is opaque for duplicate variables. Fileflow and Cloudsignal are generic; Sarraf has an indirect appraisal association without a clear duplicate-variable link.
Verospec survives on both sides. Mihenk evokes validation more directly than Koru, which suggests protection. The new reader does not create an advantage here.
Both lists drift toward generic release/build imagery. PureSiz exposes the inherited sizes-to-siz stemming problem; Multain is too opaque for binary-size comparison.
Polinter, Liginter, Sevnect and Storter feel constructed; Storeseed and Queryflow describe storage/querying more than recovery by transaction replay.
Izci is short and has a clear tracking association for a Turkish-speaking owner. It still does not communicate certificate expiry. Old candidates primarily describe the terminal wrapper.
Browsr is shared and generic. Other candidates do not provide a convincing readable accessibility-diagnosis identity. The new keyword budget also loses form behind rendered.
Tracepeak is readable and relates to the stack-trace material. Reportloom is another broad report compound; Halka expresses grouping but lacks the crash-trace identity on both sides.
The same cartographic name remains the strongest option. Changing Routelink to Docsignal offers no clear aesthetic or functional benefit.

limitations: The implementing assistant saw arm labels; these are not human or blind responses.
No repeat-consistency or promotion gate is scored.
Izci is a provisional choice with Turkish-language associations, not demonstrated international appeal.
No current availability or trademark checks were performed.
Do not train or retune thresholds from these choices.
